_meta.description: Reasoned Stage 4 adjustments after boundary and sense-consistency review.
_meta.semantics: Positive values add a penalty; negative values reduce automatic penalties.

absorb--0--v.reason: general cross-context meaning; chemical and physical wording describes the mechanism rather than a narrow field

accident--0--n.reason: highly familiar everyday concept below the B2-C1 target despite broad frequency

act--1--v.reason: basic action verb; objective frequency and polysemy otherwise dominate the Tier 2 signal

agree--0--v.reason: foundational conversational verb rather than a distinctly Tier 2 item

believe--0--v.reason: foundational everyday cognition verb already well below the target learning level

bright--1--adj.reason: primary light-emission sense is basic; abstract later senses would be more Tier 2-like

build--1--v.reason: primary physical-construction sense is foundational vocabulary

burn--1--v.reason: primary fire sense is foundational concrete vocabulary

change--1--v.reason: primary make-different sense is foundational vocabulary

cover--1--v.reason: primary put-on-top sense is foundational concrete vocabulary

decay--1--v.reason: broad process verb across everyday and academic contexts; biological agents do not make the sense purely technical

flood--0--n.reason: common concrete natural-event noun rather than a high-leverage Tier 2 concept

fresh--1--adj.reason: primary recently-produced sense is familiar foundational vocabulary

repeat--1--v.reason: primary say-again sense is foundational classroom and everyday vocabulary

soil--0--n.reason: common concrete material noun rather than a cross-context Tier 2 concept

symbol--1--n.reason: general representational concept; chemical notation is only one example in the definition

weak--0--adj.reason: primary lack-of-physical-strength sense is foundational vocabulary
